text:
Maria: quick follow-up from the handoff meeting — I'm worried our current 'capability manifest' is too coarse. in practice hosted/dedicated/private need different surface granularity for auth, KV cache layout, and fallback routing. can we clarify what should live in the minimal handshake vs what stays implementation-specific?
Kevin: absolutely. can you sketch the split you have in mind?
Maria: sure. proposal: minimal handshake = identity, model compatibility labels, required runtime hooks (kv-cache, streaming), and a probe endpoint. everything else (autoscale hints, node-pools, secret backends) stays opaque. example manifest: 
```
capabilities: [
  {name: "identity", version: "v1"},
  {name: "model-compat", tags: ["quantized", "kv-v2"]},
  {name: "probe", endpoint: "/_health?probe=handshake"},
  {name: "streaming", streams: ["chunked", "event"]}
]
policies: {fallback: ["region", "compatible-variant"]}
```
Priya: +1 to probe + minimal labels. ops teams hate big manifests that leak infra details. we should keep secret backends out.
Jamal: question — how do we encode 'compatible-variant'? that seems policy-heavy.
Maria: good point. my thought: compatibility labels are just capability flags (e.g., 'kv-v2', 'fast-attn') and routing policy evaluates those flags. policy language stays in control plane, not in the manifest. manifest only advertises flags.
Kevin: that keeps adapter surface small. but we need explicit contract for the probe semantics: if probe returns 204 => ready, 409 => needs migration, 5xx => transient. document those codes.
Alex: tiny nit — streaming has latency constraints. manifest should allow optional SLO hints (p50/p95) so router can prefer low-latency pools for sync flows. but mark SLO hints as advisory only.
Priya: agree. advisory SLOs are fine. please don't make routing depend on advisory fields for correctness.
Maria: noted. also: for private deployments we should allow a 'quirks' free-form string to capture required operational notes (e.g., air-gapped=false). keep it human readable; control plane shouldn't parse it.
Jamal: how do we handle secret rotation? if manifest is minimal and opaque about secret backends, we still need a way to signal credential refresh windows.
Kevin: add a single timestamp field 'credentials_expires_at' in handshake. that's all control plane needs to schedule refresh. actual rotation mechanism is local.
Maria: perfect. proposed v0 handshake fields: identity, capability_flags, probe_endpoint, credentials_expires_at, advisory_slo. leave everything else in host-specific metadata.
Alex: can we make the probe idempotent and cheap? some on-prem probes hit huge caches and spike CPU. recommend a shallow /_handshake end that only checks ingress+kv-header.
deploy-bot: deployment-check: manifest-schema:v0 validated for 3/4 adapters (hosted,dedicated,private).
Priya: next actions: 1) draft one-pager with fields & semantics, 2) add probe status codes to ops runbook, 3) run compatibility sweep on current adapters. I'll take 1 and 2.
Maria: thanks — I'll open the one-pager PR with examples and an integration test harness. tagging @Kevin for the compatibility sweep.
Kevin: will run sweep next week. if we can keep the handshake lean we avoid a million adapter churns :thumbsup:
Maria: ok closing here. we'll iterate in RFC but this gives a direction: minimal, probe-first, flags-only compatibility, advisory SLOs, creds window.
Alex: sounds good. :rocket:
